strengths: Insightful and well-motivated empirical analysis connecting visual scene complexity (measured via edge and color entropy metrics) to attention dispersion and downstream reasoning errors in vision-language models.

The proposed CARVE method is training-free and conceptually elegant, formalizing attention filtering via a contrastive objective between task-specific and general prompts under a multiplicative noise assumption.

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation across seven diverse benchmarks (e.g., TextVQA, V*, POPE, A-OKVQA, DocVQA, ChartQA, ScienceQA) and multiple model families/scales (LLaVA-1.5, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, Gemma-3), demonstrating consistent accuracy gains.

Thorough ablations and honest discussion of limitations, including mathematical derivations, empirical validation of the multiplicative decomposition, prompt sensitivity analysis, and failure case demonstration on global spatial reasoning tasks (BLINK).
weaknesses: Inference latency is substantially increased: requiring up to three forward passes (even with early exit for intermediate layers) roughly triples GPU execution time, which limits efficiency in real-time or compute-constrained deployment scenarios.

Pixel-level cropping and masking inherently degrades performance on queries requiring global contextual or holistic spatial reasoning (e.g., relative depth and global spatial layouts), making the technique dependent on prior knowledge of whether the task requires localized versus global visual cues.

The theoretical framing based on an element-wise multiplicative decomposition ($A^{(Q)} \approx F_{\text{vis}} \otimes F_{\text{sem}}$) is an idealized heuristic that overlooks the complex, non-linear softmax normalizations and query-key dot-product dynamics of multi-layer Transformer attention.

strengths: Compelling Empirical Motivation: The paper provides clear quantitative evidence linking visual complexity (measured via texture and color entropy) to attention dispersion and reasoning degradation in vision-language models.

Principled Formulation: The contrastive attention refinement method is derived through an intuitive multiplicative decomposition and regularized optimization formulation, resulting in an elegant closed-form normalization rule.

Comprehensive Experimental Evaluation: The method is extensively evaluated across seven diverse benchmarks (A-OKVQA, POPE, V*, TextVQA, DocVQA, ChartQA, ScienceQA) and multiple model families (LLaVA-1.5, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, Gemma-3), yielding consistent and significant performance gains without task-specific training.

Thorough Analysis and Ablation: The paper thoroughly ablates design choices (layer selection, time steps, contrastive vs. additive, hyperparameter sensitivity) and compares favorably against both external tool baselines (SAM, YOLO) and recent cropping approaches (ViCrop, SD-RPN).
Constructive Discussion of Limitations: The authors transparently analyze failure modes on global spatial reasoning tasks (e.g., depth ordering in BLINK) and quantify computational overheads.
weaknesses: Inference Overhead: The approach requires multiple forward passes (general instruction, question-specific attention extraction, and final inference), approximately tripling the inference compute and latency compared to standard single-pass generation.

Simplified Attention Independence Assumption: Modeling attention weights as a direct element-wise product of visual noise and semantic factor ($A^{(Q)} = F_{vis} \otimes F_{sem}$) is an idealized simplification that overlooks the non-linear softmax normalization across tokens in multi-head cross-attention.

Sensitivity to Global Context: By design, cropping and masking spatially suppress background context, which intrinsically risks discarding critical global relational or perspective cues, as evidenced by the BLINK failure case.

strengths: Insightful empirical analysis connecting image complexity (quantified via Canny edge density and HSV hue entropy) to visual attention dispersion (Shannon entropy) and demonstrating that higher attention dispersion correlates with performance drops.

Well-motivated contrastive attention concept: using a task-agnostic prompt to capture image-intrinsic visual clutter/noise and normalizing the task-specific attention map to isolate task-relevant semantic regions.

Solid empirical evaluation across multiple benchmarks (TextVQA, V*, POPE, A-OKVQA, DocVQA, ChartQA, ScienceQA) and multiple model architectures (LLaVA-1.5 and Qwen2.5-VL), showing consistent accuracy gains over vanilla baselines and related cropping approaches like ViCrop.

Comprehensive ablation and sensitivity experiments, including investigations of temporal token selection, layer fusion depths, general prompt variations, multiplicative versus additive contrast formulations, and hyperparameter stability ($p$ and $K$).
Transparent discussion of limitations and failure modes, specifically analyzing cases where physical background masking breaks global scene context (e.g., relative depth perception on BLINK).
weaknesses: High inference computational cost: CARVE requires three separate forward passes (general instruction, question attention extraction, and final inference on the cropped/masked image), resulting in roughly 3x to 4x higher inference latency and GPU time compared to vanilla inference.

The theoretical framing is somewhat overstated: the multiplicative decomposition assumption ($A^{(Q)} = F_{vis} \otimes F_{sem}$) is an idealized heuristic simplification that overlooks the complex non-linear softmax dynamics of transformer attention, making the formal proofs in the appendix primarily algebraic manipulations of postulated scalar objectives rather than rigorous theoretical guarantees.

Dependence on heuristic visual post-processing: the pipeline relies on several sequential filtering heuristics (percentile thresholding, connected components analysis, cropping, and resizing) with multiple hyperparameters ($p, K, \lambda$) that may require task-specific tuning across diverse visual domains.

Limited applicability to global visual reasoning tasks: because the approach relies on masking/cropping background clutter, it is primarily effective for localized perception (OCR, small-object finding) and can degrade performance on holistic or relational visual tasks that depend on global context.
